Jagdish vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 19 January, 2023
Author: Anjuli Palo
Bench: Anjuli Palo
In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh At Jabalpur Cra No. 8086 of 2022 (Jagdish
Vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh) Dated : 19-01-2023 Shri Sankalp Kochar - Advocate for
the appellant.

entities.text: High Court Of Madhya Pradesh At Jabalpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Ms. Sunita Sood - Panel Lawyer for the State.
Heard on I.A.No.17266/2022, which is first application filed on behalf of the appellant for suspension of sentence and grant of bail.
T h e appellant has been convicted by the trial Court under Sections 376(2)(G) of IPC and sentenced to R.I. for 10 years with fine of Rs.1000/- with default stipulation.

Learned counsel for the appellant has submitted that the trial Court has not properly appreciated the oral and documentary evidence available on record and committed error in convicting the appellant for aforesaid offences.

The appellant has been falsely implicated in the case due to previous enmity because husband of the prosecutrix was also arrested by the Police for commission of rape upon the sister of the present appellant.
This fact has been admitted by the prosecutrix in her cross-examination.
It is further submitted that jail sentence of co-accused Chunna has already been suspended by coordinate Bench of this Court vide order dated 13.3.2014.
Case of the present appellant is similar to him.

It is further submitted that the appellant is in custody and there is a bleak possibility of disposal of this appeal in near future, therefore, the custodial sentence of the appellant may be suspended and he may be released on bail on the ground of parity.
Learned Panel Lawyer has opposed the prayer for bail.
I have heard learned counsel for the parties.
Looking to the overall facts and circumstances of the case and maintaining parity with co-accused Chunnilal @ Munna, without commenting on the merit of the case, the application is allowed.

I t is directed that subject to depositing the fine amount, if not already deposited and on furnishing a personal bond in a sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned, the custodial sentence of appellant Jagdish shall remain suspended and he shall be released on bail for securing his presence before the trial Court on 6.7.2023 and on such other dates as may be fixed in this regard during pendency of this appeal.
